In [[geometry]], the '''triaugmented hexagonal prism''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|57}}}}). As the name suggests, it can be constructed by triply augmenting a hexagonal [[prism (geometry)|prism]] by attaching [[square pyramid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|1}}}}) to three of its nonadjacent equatorial faces.
